info.name: Competition Web App API v1
info.description: REST API v1 serving the Competition Web App data (areas, parameters, timeseries, map layers and their values, forecasts, hazards, basemap). Full reference: server/docs/API.md. Set the baseUrl variable to point at another server. Expected status for each request is in its description.

request.description: Service status, versions and data timestamp. Expect 200. Never cached.
Label, unit, decimals, aggregation and intervals of every series key. Expect 200.
One parameter by key. Expect 200.

item.name: Areas
item.description: Places the API has data for (cities today).

request.description: Every area with region, center and data coverage. Expect 200.

item.name: List cities with boundary and layers

request.description: type filter plus embedded extras (include=* gives all). Expect 200.
One area. Expect 200.
One area with its map layers embedded. Expect 200.
District outline as a GeoJSON Feature. Expect 200.

item.name: Timeseries
item.description: Monthly series for one or many areas.

request.description: NDVI and rainfall for two cities, Jan 2015 to Dec 2020 inclusive. Missing months are null. Expect 200.
Every area and every parameter for the full range. Expect 200.
type filters areas=* like on /areas (what the website loads at startup). Expect 200.
No area has type custom yet, so data.areas is {}. Expect 200.
One area; parameters default to all. A range reaching outside the data is clipped. Expect 200.

item.name: Layers
item.description: Map layers and the per-pixel values behind them.

request.description: Map layers of an area: bounds, times, image paths, values link. Expect 200.
Jaisalmer also has three Sentinel-2 10 m image layers. Expect 200.
One layer. Expect 200.
Stored integer grid for 2020; multiply by scale (0.001) for NDVI. Expect 200.
A timed layer without time returns every year: { "2010": grid, ... }. Expect 200.
time is written in the layer's interval (ndvi-peak: yearly, YYYY). Expect 200.
Summer daytime land surface temperature grid; multiply by 0.1 for °C. Expect 200.

NDVI, 12 months, every model (ridge, nn, gbm), computed from the area's Earth Engine table (data/gee/jaipur.features.csv, the team notebook's pipeline). The first request per area takes a few seconds while the models train; repeats come from the cache. data.source is "live", or "snapshot" when the Python module cannot run. Expect 200 once the area has been extracted (npm run gee:extract); before that 503 forecast_unavailable with details.reason "no_gee_data".
Same question written out: one parameter, horizon in months (1-24), models list. Jaisalmer is the notebook's own area. Expect 200 (503 no_gee_data until extracted).
Models always come back in the order ridge, nn, gbm. Expect 200 (503 no_gee_data until extracted).
Hazard types (flood today) and what each provides: events, daily parameters, observations, and the forecast with its danger classes, models and thresholds. Expect 200.

One hazard plus its dataset (tables and their columns, source datasets and citations, notes) and the forecast model: thresholds, out-of-fold and held-out test scores, threshold sweep, feature importance, which events trained and tested it, and the check against the notebook. Expect 200.

What can be plotted for a flood event: daily rainfall series (box average, wettest cell, 3- and 7-day totals), the reported-flood-period flag, and the soil moisture passes (kind "observation"). Labels, units, sources. Expect 200.
One parameter, with the context columns that come with each observation (track, phase, ...). Expect 200.

Every flood event: name, country, admin area, period, bbox [west, south, east, north], center, cause, data coverage, and whether and how it has a forecast (Nepal: excluded, not a rain flood). Expect 200 with 10 events.
Filter by ISO country code or name, case-insensitive. Expect 200 with the two Bihar events and Chattogram.
Events whose box overlaps west,south,east,north (degrees; west > east crosses the antimeridian). Expect 200 with Pakistan, Nepal, Patna, Bhagalpur and Chattogram.
One event with notes, a summary (rain before and during the flood, soil passes), attributes, sources (citations and source files) and links. Expect 200.
Every event with its map layers embedded (data[].layers); coverage.layers lists the layer ids of each event ([] when none). Expect 200.
One event plus its full layer objects in data.layers. Expect 200.
Every parameter: data.series holds the daily series aligned with data.times; data.observations holds the soil moisture passes, each with its own times, values and context. Expect 200.
Chosen parameters and an inclusive UTC date range (YYYY-MM-DD). The 3-day total on the first day still counts the days before it. Expect 200 with 15 days.

Per day: each model's probability of the flood within the next 3 days, its threshold and the danger class (probability >= threshold), the actual outcome, the inputs, and the scores. A held-out test event, scored by the final model (evaluation.role "test"). Expect 200.
A training event is scored out-of-fold (evaluation.role "out_of_fold"; fold and foldEvents say which cross-validation model held it out). One model, days from 1 Jan. Expect 200.
Nepal is kept as data but left out of the model, as in the notebook (a glacier collapse, not rain). Expect 200 with data.available false and evaluation.reason.

The event's map layers: today the reference water extent (water-reference) of the notebook's Part A labels, with bounds [[south, west], [north, east]], legend, stats (water km², % of known pixels, unknown %, inside the event box), source and the image url. Expect 200 with meta.count 1. An event without layers returns [].
One layer. data.url is the overlay PNG on this API (prefix the API origin); its ?v= is the image hash. Expect 200.
The overlay PNG itself (Content-Type image/png, Cache-Control public, max-age=86400, ETag). Transparent except water (#1a5cff at 80%). Expect 200.

item.name: Basemap
item.description: Satellite mosaics shown under the map.

request.description: Bounds, zoom, image and label paths of every mosaic. Expect 200.

item.name: Errors
item.description: Examples of every error code. Expected status is in each description.

request.description: Expect 404 not_found.
Expect 400 invalid_parameter (details.unknown, details.valid).
areas is required on /timeseries. Expect 400 invalid_query.
from must be YYYY-MM for monthly data. Expect 400 invalid_query.
Expect 400 invalid_query.
Expect 400 invalid_query (details.allowed).
Only monthly exists today. Expect 400 unsupported_interval (details.supported).
yearly describes layer times, it is not a timeseries interval. Expect 400 unsupported_interval (details.supported = ["monthly"]).

A parameter named in the list must offer the interval; otherwise 400 unsupported_interval with details { interval, parameter, supported } (with parameters=* such parameters are left out instead). Every parameter is monthly today, so this query only shows the shape. Expect 200.

areas x parameters x times above the limit (TIMESERIES_MAX_VALUES, default 500000) is 400 invalid_query with details.limit and details.requested. The full data is 6 x 16 x 201 = 19296 values, so this needs a server started with a small limit, e.g. TIMESERIES_MAX_VALUES=1000 npm start. Expect 400 invalid_query there, 200 with the default.
Well formed (YYYY) but not in the layer's times. Expect 404 not_found (details.times).
ndvi-peak is yearly, so a month is the wrong format. Expect 400 invalid_query (details.format = "YYYY").
Static layers have one grid. Expect 400 invalid_query.
Sentinel-2 layers are images only. Expect 404 not_found.
Expect 404 not_found.

item.name: Forecast: parameter that cannot be forecast

request.description: rain exists but has no forecast model. Expect 400 invalid_parameter (details.unforecastable, details.valid = ["ndvi"]).
One parameter per request. Expect 400 invalid_query.
horizon is a whole number from 1 to 24. Expect 400 invalid_query (details.min, details.max).
Expect 400 invalid_query (details.unknown, details.allowed = ["ridge", "nn", "gbm"]).
Forecasts are monthly only. Expect 400 unsupported_interval (details.supported = ["monthly"]).

An area whose Earth Engine table (data/gee/<id>.features.csv) has not been extracted yet. Expect 503 forecast_unavailable with details.reason "no_gee_data" and a message saying so (200 once npm run gee:extract has run for it).

Needs an area with an extracted table and a server that cannot run Python: FORECAST_MODE=snapshot npm start (or FORECAST_PYTHON=/nonexistent). Expect 503 forecast_unavailable (details.saved) when no saved forecast covers 18 months; with one from npm run forecasts:build (24 months) 200 with data.source "snapshot"; 200 live with the module installed in live mode.

Needs an area with an extracted table and a module that fails: FORECAST_PYTHON=/usr/bin/false npm start. Without a saved forecast expect 502 model_failure; with one, 200 with data.source "snapshot" and meta.fallback "model_failure". 200 live with a working module.
Expect 404 not_found (details.valid lists the hazards).
Expect 404 not_found (details.hazard, details.eventId).
Expect 400 invalid_parameter (details.unknown, details.valid).
Hazard series are daily. Expect 400 invalid_query (details.format = "YYYY-MM-DD").
Expect 400 unsupported_interval (details.supported = ["daily"]).
Expect 400 invalid_query (details.format = "west,south,east,north").
Expect 400 invalid_query (details.allowed = ["rain", "rain_soil"]).

Only when server/data/hazards/flood/model/forecast.json is missing (the model has not been built: python -m forecaster.hazards build flood): 503 forecast_unavailable with details.reason "no_model". Expect 200 with the committed data.
Expect 404 not_found (details.layerId, details.valid = ["water-reference"]).
Events offer include=layers only. Expect 400 invalid_query (details.allowed = ["layers"]).
Only GET (and HEAD) are supported. Expect 405 method_not_allowed with an Allow header.
Expect 404 not_found. (The old unversioned /api/... endpoints are gone too.)
